Slope of the log relative wage on log relative supply

blocks.md: The elasticity of substitution measures how readily a producer swaps one input for another when their relative price changes. If skilled workers become 10% more expensive relative to unskilled ones and firms respond by cutting their relative use of skilled workers by 20%, the elasticity is 2: the two are easy to swap. If firms barely change their mix, the elasticity is small and the inputs are complements that have to be used together.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.md: It determines how far a group's wages fall when that group becomes more plentiful, and whether new technology helps or hurts the skill premium.
The percentage change in relative input use for a 1% change in relative input prices:
Equivalently, the inverse governs how the relative wage responds to relative supply:

- **High $\sigma$**: skilled and unskilled workers are close substitutes. Firms switch easily, so a large increase in college graduates barely dents the premium.
- **Low $\sigma$**: they are complements. Extra college graduates sharply lower their own relative wage.

It governs (1) how much a supply increase lowers the [Skill Premium](note:skill-premium) and (2) whether skill-augmenting technology *raises* the premium at all — that requires $\sigma > 1$ ([Factor-Augmenting Technology](note:factor-augmenting-technology)).

In the [Canonical Model of the Skill Premium](note:canonical-model-of-the-skill-premium), $\sigma$ is recovered from the coefficient on $\ln(H/L)$: $\beta = -1/\sigma$. This is a log-log coefficient, read as an elasticity exactly as in [Functional Forms and Elasticities](note:functional-forms-and-elasticities).
See [Elasticity of Substitution Between College and Non-College Labor](note:elasticity-of-substitution-between-college-and-non-college-labor) for estimates.

- Math background: [Logarithms and Growth Rates](note:logarithms-and-growth-rates)
- [CES Production Function](note:ces-production-function)
- [Relative Supply and Demand](note:relative-supply-and-demand) — $-1/\sigma$ is the slope of the relative demand curve in logs
